thread:
maria: Quick readout from the usability sessions on the API keys modal — surfacing some small but recurring friction points around permissions and the rotate/revoke affordances. TL;DR: people want clearer defaults, clearer consequences for broad scopes, and better focus/announce behavior for the secret reveal drawer.

josh: Nice — can you call out the top 3 exact changes we should try in the next build?

maria: Sure: 1) Add a compact ‘permission scaffold’ drop-down with presets (Read-only, Embeddings-only, Admin-lite). 2) Inline warning when someone picks anything that includes *write* + *admin* (tone: neutral, actionable). 3) Improve keyboard flow when the secret is shown (move focus to the copy button, announce "secret revealed" via aria-live).

olivia: For the presets — are those just labels or do they pre-check a set of individual toggles? I worry about users not understanding what the preset contains.

maria: Presets should expand an inline summary when hovered/clicked: small sentence like "Embeddings-only: can run embed endpoints, cannot generate completions or manage keys". We experimented with both tooltip and inline expandable row; users preferred inline text because tooltips were missed.

samir: From an impl POV, presets that map to a list of boolean flags is easy. Question: do we persist last-used preset per org or per user? Persisting per org could surprise small teams.

maria: Good point — default to org-level but show a soft hint: "Using org default: Embeddings-only — change for this key" with an ephemeral toggle to override. That avoids accidental drift.

aisha: Accessibility nit: when toggles expand the permission details, ensure we 1) use aria-expanded on the toggle, 2) move focus into the details if the user used keyboard to open, and 3) ensure the warning text is read by screen readers (use an aria-live polite region for the warning).

josh: UX question about the inline warning copy — what wording did research prefer? We tried a few variations.

maria: Participants responded best to concrete examples. Avoid vague "high risk" phrasing. Suggested: "This key grants token creation and model generation. Consider choosing a scoped preset or limiting access to a specific service account." Then a small link: "Learn more about scopes".

olivia: Can we add a micro-copy confirmation on rotate? e.g., when rotating, show a small risk summary: "Rotating will invalidate existing tokens in X minutes — update any running jobs" with a 1-click copy-to-clipboard of the new secret. Should be subtle but above the fold.

samir: Implementation note: rotation endpoint already returns the new secret once; we should ensure the UI surfaces it in a banner with a single CTA to copy, plus a checkbox "Log rotation event to audit log" default on for org-admins.

aisha: Also: when the secret drawer opens, the reveal should be announced like "API key secret displayed. Use Copy to copy to clipboard. This secret will not be shown again." That small message reduced confusion in testing.

designbot: quick mock suggestion: replace the full modal footer CTA "Create key" with a two-step affordance — primary "Create key (show secret)" and a secondary small chevron to expand advanced options (presets, expiration, notes). Keeps the modal shorter and surfaces presets only when needed. :sparkles:

josh: I like that. One more ask: make the perms matrix compact on small screens — condense toggles into a single-select list when viewport < 520px.

maria: Agreed. I'll update the Figma with the scaffold dropdown, inline details, and the rotate banner copy. I'll also add aria notes for a11y.

olivia: Thanks — can you drop the updated frames into #design-review by EOD? I'll schedule a quick sync with eng to triage implementation complexity.

maria: Yep — dropping in now. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
